headline: Philippine Inflation Hits 44-Month High on Rising Fuel Costs
summary: Inflation in the Philippines reached 7.8% in October, the highest level in 44 months, driven by soaring petrol prices linked to Middle East conflict and a devalued peso.
why: High inflation erodes consumer purchasing power and often forces central banks to raise interest rates, which can slow economic growth.

impacts.name: Philippine Peso
impacts.why: High inflation and currency devaluation often lead to further downward pressure on the local currency.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Inflation data exceeding expectations typically triggers market concerns regarding central bank policy tightening and currency stability.
